dataset.name: SUMO Chamber Conditions
description: The Los Alamos Survival–Mortality experiment (SUMO) is located on Frijoles Mesa near Los Alamos, New Mexico, USA, at an elevation of 2150 m. This was a tree manipulation study that investigated the relative impacts of drought and warming on plant function and reveals how trees adapt to drought and heat in semi-arid regions. The study factored the role of tree hydraulic acclimation to both precipitation and temperature and separated their effects.The experiment is located in a pinon-juniper woodland near the ponderosa pine (Pinus ponderosa) forest ecotone.

Chamber conditions (temperature, relative humidity, vapor pressure deficit) for SUMO Open Top Chambers (OTCs) used to control air temperatures surrounding heated and control chamber trees. See SUMO Target Tree Information data package (doi:10.15485/1440544) for additional information. Data released by Los Alamos National Lab for public use under LA-UR-18-23656.

measurementTechnique: The temperature treatment was implemented with 18 transparent, open-top chambers (OTCs) regulated by heating and cooling units (RJPL Package Heat Pump and RLPL Package Air Conditioner; Rheem Manufacturing Company, Atlanta, GA, USA) to enable temperature control (Garcia-Forner et al., 2015). OTCs maintained at ambient temperatures allowed testing for any chamber effects independent of heating. Chamber conditions (air temperature and relative humidity) were monitored by two sets of sensors in each chamber: one at 1 m and one at 2/3 tree height using Campbell CS215 Temperature and Relative Humidity Probe (Campbell Scientific, Logan UT, USA). The data was collected every 5 min on a Campbell CR1000 data logger. This system was used as a thermostat to set desired temperature conditions in chambers. Here the data is further averaged to give daily average values for each chamber.
